faqs.a: Yes, but only through the aviation route. The Warrant Officer Flight Training program accepts qualified civilians with no prior military service, provided they meet the age, citizenship, education, GT and SIFT requirements and pass the flight physical. All other warrant officer specialties normally require enlisted service first.
faqs.q: Can a civilian become an Army warrant officer without prior service?

faqs.a: You need a General Technical score of 110 or higher on the ASVAB, with no waiver available, and a SIFT score of 40 or higher. The SIFT tests spatial reasoning, mathematics, reading comprehension and basic aviation knowledge, so preparation in all four areas matters before you sit the test.
faqs.q: What scores do I need for WOFT?

faqs.a: For WOFT, you must be between 18 and 33 at the time of board selection, with age waivers considered case by case. Technical warrant officer applicants are generally aged 18 to 46, and aviation applicants must be programmed to begin flight training before turning 33.
faqs.q: How old can I be to apply as a warrant officer?

faqs.a: After Warrant Officer Candidate School, WOFT students complete about 32 weeks of Initial Entry Rotary Wing training, totalling roughly 179 flight hours before earning their wings. Technical warrant officers complete specialty courses of varying length, followed by a service obligation agreed at appointment.
faqs.q: How long is warrant officer training?

headline: Become a US Army Warrant Officer in 2026
metaDescription: Complete 2026 guide to US Army warrant officer recruitment: WOFT and technical paths, age limits, GT 110 and SIFT scores, fitness, medical standards and boards.

sections.content:
Most Army warrant officers are promoted from the enlisted ranks, usually as senior non-commissioned officers with years of hands-on technical experience in their specialty. They compete before a selection board with a recommendation package, a strong service record and the qualifications for their chosen military occupational specialty.

The major exception is Army aviation. The Warrant Officer Flight Training (WOFT) program is one of the only warrant officer routes open to civilians with no prior military service, letting qualified applicants train directly to fly Army helicopters.
sections.title: Two Routes to Warrant Officer

sections.content:
Civilian WOFT applicants must be US citizens aged 18 to 33 at board selection, hold a high school diploma and meet Army height and weight standards. They need a General Technical (GT) score of 110 or higher on the ASVAB, with no waiver for that requirement, and a passing score of 40 or higher on the Selection Instrument for Flight Training (SIFT).

Applicants must also pass a Class 1A flight physical, the Army's most demanding aviation medical standard, and obtain a secret security clearance. A selection board reviews each packet, including letters of recommendation, and boards convene several times a year.
sections.title: WOFT Eligibility and Tests

sections.content:
Technical warrant officer applicants generally need to hold at least the rank of E-5, with four to six years of experience in a closely related specialty, and have at least 12 months remaining on their enlistment contract. The technical age window runs from 18 to 46, with waivers possible above that age in some cases.

Selected candidates attend Warrant Officer Candidate School, followed by specialty training. WOFT graduates complete roughly 32 weeks of Initial Entry Rotary Wing flight training, about 179 flight hours, before earning their wings and accepting a multi-year service obligation.
